references.text: Isaiah prophesies that God will besiege Jerusalem, set up camp against the city, and build siege ramps—the same image Jesus uses in [ref:Jes 29:3-4|Isaiah 29:3-4]: "I will set up camp against you all around, and I will besiege you with ramparts."
Jeremiah describes how the enemy will cut down trees and build a siege ramp against Jerusalem, paralleling Jesus' words about siege ramps ([ref:Jer 6:6|Jeremiah 6:6]).

Ezekiel is told to depict the siege of Jerusalem with a model—to set up camp against the city, build ramparts, and lay siege to it from all sides, as Jesus describes in [ref:Esek 4:1-3|Ezekiel 4:1-3].
In [ref:Jes 37:33|Isaiah 37:33], there is mention of building a siege ramp against Jerusalem, using the same expression (χάρακα) that Jesus uses regarding the coming destruction.

Jesus later repeats the same prophecy about the destruction of Jerusalem in [ref:Luk 21:20|Luke 21:20], saying that when they see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then they will know that its destruction is near.
In [ref:Luk 21:24|Luke 21:24], Jesus expands on the prophecy by stating that Jerusalem will be trampled down by Gentile nations, continuing the siege motif from Luke 19:43.

Moses warns Israel that enemies will besiege them in all their gates and press them from every direction, reflecting the expression "from all sides" (πάντοθεν) in Jesus' prophecy ([ref:5 Mos 28:52|Deuteronomy 28:52]).
Isaiah prophesies about Jerusalem's sorrow under judgment, where the city gates will mourn—an image of the coming destruction that Jesus warns about here ([ref:Jes 3:26|Isaiah 3:26]).
Hosea declares that the days of reckoning and retribution have come—parallel to Jesus' words "days will come upon you" ([ref:Hos 9:7|Hosea 9:7]).
The following verse [ref:Luk 19:44|Luke 19:44] expands on the siege imagery by describing the total destruction that will follow, and the reason: "because you did not know your time of visitation."
